title: Whole Known, Parts Known
objective: Build and verify a bond when both the whole and both parts are already known — the straightforward case, before any part is missing.
studentQuestion: Does everything in this bond agree?
newIdea: Verifying a fully-known bond is internally consistent (parts add to the whole) — sets up recognizing when something is missing next.

teaching.setup: A bond with the whole and both parts filled in, sometimes correct, sometimes deliberately wrong (e.g. whole 9, parts 5 and 3).
teaching.see: Every number in this bond is already filled in. Is it correct?
teaching.break: Add the two parts together independently of what the bond claims the whole is.
teaching.build: Compare the computed sum to the stated whole.
teaching.transform: A broken bond, corrected into a true one — same numbers rearranged into a form that's actually consistent.

check.prompt: Rebuild with objects if the bond is in question.

examples.second: A deliberately incorrect bond (9 claimed, but parts are 5 and 3).
examples.transfer: The learner builds their own fully-known, correct bond from a chosen whole.

mastery.evidence: Correctly identifies at least one true and one false bond, with justification.
